vision.description: Set the direction before you design the solution
vision.whatIsIt: Vision for Change sets out why AVT matters, how it will improve patient care and staff experience and what good looks like in everyday clinical and administrative work.
vision.userInsight: AVT landed best when it was framed as a clinical workflow and behaviour change, not a technology rollout
vision.whyThisMatters:
Reduces confusion about what AVT is (and isn't) and protects trust in the change early.
 Prevents the programme being judged only on technology rather than the intended workflow improvement.
 Provides a consistent narrative across clinical, operational and admin audiences, reducing rumour-driven resistance.
vision.quickRealityCheck:
Can staff describe AVT in one sentence? Does it reflect real pressures, not just programme goals?
 Are leaders saying the same thing consistently? Do people understand what will change in their day-to-day work?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CLEAR AND COMPELLING
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Vision is simple, inspiring and focused on patient care, staff experience and better ways of working.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: UNDERSTOOD AND SHARED
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Staff at all levels can explain in their own words why AVT matters and what will change..

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CONSISTENTLY COMMUNICATED
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Leaders reinforce the vision regularly and use it to guide decisions and priorities.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: GROUNDED IN REAL SITUATIONS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Vision reflects the day-to-day challenges teams face and the improvements AVT will bring.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: GUIDES ACTIONS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Vision helps teams make choices, solve problems and stay focused on what matters

risksIfYouDont.title: SEEN AS A TECHNOLOGY ROLLOUT
risksIfYouDont.body: Focus stays on the tool rather than the workflow and behaviour change.

risksIfYouDont.title: CONFUSION AND MIXED MESSAGES
risksIfYouDont.body: Different teams hear different things, leading to uncertainty about the reason AVT is being introduced.

risksIfYouDont.title: LOW ENGAGEMENT AND RESISTANCE
risksIfYouDont.body: Staff don't see the relevance to their day-to-day work and are less likely to adopt AVT.

risksIfYouDont.title: INCONSISTENT ADOPTION
risksIfYouDont.body: Without a shared vision, use will vary widely across teams and services.

risksIfYouDont.title: BENEFITS NOT REALISED
risksIfYouDont.body: Without a clear direction, efforts drift and the value of AVT is not achieved

case_for_change.description: AVT must solve a problem that staff clearly recognise
case_for_change.whatIsIt: A Case for Change explains the real clinical and operational pressures AVT is responding to, why change is needed now and why current  Ways of working are becoming unsustainable.
case_for_change.userInsight: AVT was most effective when it clearly addressed real operational pressures such as backlogs, wait times and admin burdens.
case_for_change.whyThisMatters: Prevents confusion over whether AVT is about productivity, wellbeing, backlog reduction or system replacement. Helps teams agree on the workflow changes needed to realise the benefits. Reduces early resistance by focusing on the problem that needs solving, not the novelty of AVT.
case_for_change.quickRealityCheck: Can we explain why change is needed now? Are the benefits specific and measurable? Can leaders explain the change in one simple story? Is the problem clearly defined or are you starting with AVT as the answer?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: AVT NOT SEEN AS A TECHNICAL ROLLOUT
whatGoodLooksLike.body: AVT is consistently understood as a clinical workflow and behaviour change, not a technology rollout

whatGoodLooksLike.title: LOWER COGNITIVE LOAD
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Clinicians experience lower cognitive load, better patient interaction and stronger day-to-day usability

whatGoodLooksLike.title: RESISTANCE REDUCTION
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Reduces early resistance by focusing on the problem that needs solving, not the novelty of AVT

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CLEAR PROBLEM STATEMENT
whatGoodLooksLike.body: The problem AVT is solving is specific, evidence-based and easy to explain.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: COMPELLING REASON TO ACT NOW
whatGoodLooksLike.body: There is urgency, not just a general desire to improve.

risksIfYouDont.title: STALLED ADOPTION
risksIfYouDont.body: Adoption stalls once the novelty fades because the purpose was never clear.

risksIfYouDont.title: DISENGAGEMENT
risksIfYouDont.body: Productivity narratives trigger suspicion and disengagement in AVTs introduction.

risksIfYouDont.title: SCALING JUSTIFICATION STRUGGLES
risksIfYouDont.body: Leaders struggle to justify scaling because there is no credible “why now” and “what problem”

risksIfYouDont.title: BUSINESS OUTCOMES NOT LINKED
risksIfYouDont.body: Business Outcomes are not clearly linked to AVT

risksIfYouDont.title: DISAGREEMENTS REGARDING THE PROBLEM
risksIfYouDont.body: Stakeholders do not agree on the problem statement.

sponsorship.description: Make AVT clinically led and operationally owned, not IT driven
sponsorship.whatIsIt: Sponsorship means visible clinical and operational senior leaders driving AVT as service improvement, supporting teams, removing barriers and building confidence to support adoption. Governance provides the structure for making clear timely decisions, so AVT is introduced safely, consistently and at scale by having the right clinical, digital and safety checks in place.
sponsorship.userInsight: AVT succeeded when strong clinical and operational sponsorship ensured AVT was delivered as a clinical service improvement, not an IT led change, with leaders driving adoption, behaviours and redesign. Clear proportionate governance enabled safe timely decisions and supported AVT scaling across clinical, operational and digital teams.
sponsorship.whyThisMatters:
Visible senior clinical and operational leadership builds trust, reduces resistance and enables pace and scale.
 Ensures AVT is a clinical workflow change with clinical direction and operational ownership of local redesign.
 Sponsors remove barriers, support teams and make the decisions related to risk and workflow needed to embed change.
 Drives timely and clear decisions through defined decision making, governance cadence and active oversight.
 Enables safe, compliant use by ensuring assurance (IG, DPIA, Cyber, clinical safety and consent) is in place before clinical deployment.
 Supports scaling beyond pilots by managing risks transparently and creating a controlled organisation wide approach.
sponsorship.quickRealityCheck:
Are senior leaders actively showing support? Do sponsors demonstrate behaviours they expect from others?
 Are sponsors listening to feedback and responding? Are sponsors using the same consistent story?
 Are roles clear across business, tech, legal, risk and Ops? Who actually owns the decision, risk and sign off?
 Is there a clear escalation path when something fails? Are policies being followed in practice, not just documented?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CLEAR SPONSORSHIP IN PLACE
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Clear credible sponsorship in place – named SRO, clinical sponsor (e.g. Medical Director/CCIO) and operational lead with ownership beyond digital/IT.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: VISIBLE LEADERSHIP
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Visible leadership driving change on the ground – actively engaging teams, reinforcing new behaviours and removing barriers to adoption.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: OPERATIONAL OWNERSHIP
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Operational ownership embedded early and leading workflow redesign.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: FRONTLINE FEEDBACK
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Frontline feedback is heard and acted on.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CLEAR GOVERNANCE
whatGoodLooksLike.body: There is a clear AVT governance forum aligned to existing clinical and operational structures, with clear decision rights, escalation routes and documented approval authority.

risksIfYouDont.title: FAILURE TO SCALE
risksIfYouDont.body: Without senior clinical and operational leadership, adoption depends on individual enthusiasts and fails to scale across services.

risksIfYouDont.title: NO HUMAN IN THE LOOP
risksIfYouDont.body: Workflow issues and new ways of working, including "Human in the Loop" review and approval, may not be owned or resolved.

risksIfYouDont.title: SLOW UPTAKE
risksIfYouDont.body: Without visible senior backing, teams are less confident to change practice, delaying adoption and limiting impact.

risksIfYouDont.title: DELAYED DECISION MAKING
risksIfYouDont.body: Decisions are delayed because ownership is unclear.

risksIfYouDont.title: NO GOVERNANCE
risksIfYouDont.body: Without governance, there is no clear decision making between IG, IT and clinical/operational teams, which may lead to delays, hidden risk and pilots that never transition into controlled organisation wide roll outs.

change_network.description: Use trusted peers as champions to drive adoption and improvement
change_network.whatIsIt: A Change Network brings together trusted clinical, operational and admin champions to share clear messages, surface issues early and support peer to peer adoption of AVT.
change_network.userInsight: Adoption spread through trusted peer to peer influence with champions often emerging organically who helped to drive uptake and sustain engagement over time.
change_network.whyThisMatters:
Building trust enabling two-way engagement helps to drive adoption by involving staff in the change from the start.
 Local networks help to build local confidence and support by using trusted peers.
 Champions can help to surface workflow and template issues early through frontline insight, speeding up improvements.
change_network.quickRealityCheck:
Do you have champions across the right roles, teams and locations? Do network members know what they have been asked to do?
 Has protected time been discussed and agreed with managers? Have feedback channels been set up and shared?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: VISIBLE CHAMPIONS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Champions are visible and active locally with peer learning, coaching and demonstration driving confidence and adoption as part of a Change Network.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: TWO WAY ENGAGEMENT
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Two-way engagement is working with clear, consistent messages and early feedback shaping decisions.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: USE OF INSIGHTS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Insights are used to improve rollout, with champions surfacing issues early and informing workflow and template refinement.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: SUPPORTS ADOPTION
whatGoodLooksLike.body: The network supports adoption before, during and after launch.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: HELP WITH VALIDATION
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Champions help validate real world scenarios and user impacts.

risksIfYouDont.title: LIMITED SUPPORT
risksIfYouDont.body: Limited local support and influence. Change stays centralised with no trusted peers to explain, support and encourage adoption.

risksIfYouDont.title: LOW TRUST
risksIfYouDont.body: Low trust and engagement. People don't feel involved or heard so confidence drops and resistance increases.

risksIfYouDont.title: NO PEER SUPPORT
risksIfYouDont.body: Poor adoption and inconsistent use. Without peer support and reinforcement, take up is patchy and new ways of working don't stick.

risksIfYouDont.title: LACK OF REPRESENTATION
risksIfYouDont.body: Champions are not representative of affected teams.

risksIfYouDont.title: STOPPED ACTIVITY
risksIfYouDont.body: Network activity stops after launch.

benefits.component: What's In It For Me (WIIFM) Benefits
benefits.description: Make the benefits real, relevant and meaningful for everyone
benefits.whatIsIt: What's in it for me (WIIFM) translates AVT benefits into clear, personal messages so staff can see how the change will make their own work easier or better.
benefits.userInsight: WIIFM benefits landed more effectively when they reflected real practical clinical experience – reduced cognitive load, increased patient focus and clinical safety.
benefits.whyThisMatters:
WIIFM messaging is a primary driver of engagement and can support resistance reduction.
 Role-specific benefits help reduce fear about workforce impact and job loss narratives.
 Credible WIIFM support safer adoption by reinforcing correct use and "Human in the Loop" review and approval of AVT outputs.
benefits.quickRealityCheck:
Do people understand what's in it for them? Are the benefits relevant to the real workforce pressures?
 Are we communicating WIIFM benefits in the right way? Are people showing they understand the reason for the AVT introduction?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: STAFF EXPLANATION
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Staff can explain the benefits in their own words, not just repeat generic transformation language.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: REAL DAY TO DAY IMPROVEMENTS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Communications focus on real day to day improvements.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CLEAR ADMIN IMPACTS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Admin impacts are clearly explained, including how roles may evolve and how staff will be supported.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: FEEDBACK LED ADOPTION
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Concerns are captured and used to refine messaging, training and support.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: ROLE SPECIFIC BENEFITS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Benefits are tailored by audience, especially for clinicians.

risksIfYouDont.title: DOMINATING MYTHS
risksIfYouDont.body: Productivity enforcement myths dominate and reduce uptake.

risksIfYouDont.title: INCREASED ANXIETY
risksIfYouDont.body: Admin staff assume AVT is workforce reduction leading to increased anxiety.

risksIfYouDont.title: ENTHUSIASM FADES
risksIfYouDont.body: Benefits remain theoretical; enthusiasm fades quickly.

risksIfYouDont.title: TRAINING LANDS POORLY
risksIfYouDont.body: Staff attend training but do not apply AVT because the 'Why' is unclear.

risksIfYouDont.title: MOMENTUM FADES
risksIfYouDont.body: Early interest drops off before AVT becomes embedded in ways of working.

stakeholder.description: Engage early and involve staff in shaping how AVT will work
stakeholder.whatIsIt: Stakeholder Engagement and Communications build understanding, trust and commitment through early, two-way engagement with clinicians, admin teams, leaders and patients.
stakeholder.userInsight: Adoption was strongest where trusted peers led the change, clinical and admin teams were engaged early and patients and clinicians had clarity and confidence around the change.
stakeholder.whyThisMatters:
Engagement reduces resistance by building understanding and addressing misconceptions early.
 When people are involved in design, they become advocates.
 Patient trust and understanding is increased when communication is transparent and choice based.
stakeholder.quickRealityCheck:
Is there a feedback loop after communications go out? Are comms understandable to non-technical staff?
 Are issues tracked through to closure? Are real life scenarios included in validations?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: ROLE BASED TRAINING
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Training is role-based and reinforces "Human in the Loop" review and approval of AVT outputs, with clear clinical accountability.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: AT THE ELBOW
whatGoodLooksLike.body: "At the elbow" or in-service support exists for early use and those lacking confidence.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: HELP
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Refreshers and rapid help routes exist; small irritants are fixed quickly.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: PREPARATION FOR NEW WAYS OF WORKING
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Frontline teams are prepared for new ways of working.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: PRE-GO LIVE ASSESSMENTS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Confidence and readiness are assessed before go live.

risksIfYouDont.title: NON-ADOPTION
risksIfYouDont.body: People attend training but still don't adopt because confidence is low and support isn't available.

risksIfYouDont.title: MIXED MESSAGES
risksIfYouDont.body: Mixed messages on "Human in the Loop" review and approval of AVT outputs can lead to unsafe practice or avoidance.

risksIfYouDont.title: SUPPLIER RELIANCE
risksIfYouDont.body: Reliance on suppliers persists because local super-user capability is not built.

risksIfYouDont.title: LATE IDENTIFICATION
risksIfYouDont.body: Skills gaps are identified too late.

risksIfYouDont.title: GENERIC TRAINING
risksIfYouDont.body: Training is too generic and not tailored to real use.

capability.description: Confidence grows when AVT makes work easier in practice
capability.whatIsIt: Capability and Confidence focus on building the organisational skills and confidence needed to make AVT a trusted routine part of everyday practice.
capability.userInsight: Adoption was driven by proven performance in practice through proof of concepts, whilst reliability issues quickly reduced trust.
capability.whyThisMatters:
Capability and confidence determines whether AVT becomes routine practice or use remains limited.
 Confidence supports safe "Human in the Loop" review and approval of AVT outputs, even under pressure.
 Internal capability reduces supplier dependence and helps scale up AVT.
capability.quickRealityCheck:
Can staff use AVT without step-by-step instructions? Do confidence levels match training completion?
 Have staff had safe practice time? Is peer support available locally?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: RELIABLE AVT USE
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Users can use AVT reliably in real settings and maintain full clinical responsibility through "Human in the Loop" review and approval.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CHANGE CHAMPIONS SUPPORT
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Local champions/super-users exist and are supported with customisation skills.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: IMPROVED COMPLIANCE BEHAVIOURS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Compliance behaviours (e.g. consent recording) improve through reinforcement and clearer workflows.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CONFIDENCE BUILDS GRADUALLY
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Users are supported to move from basic familiarity to confident, routine use.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: LEARNING IS REVISITED
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Training is revisited as systems, workflows or staff needs change.

risksIfYouDont.title: STALLED ADOPTION
risksIfYouDont.body: Early trust issues spread socially and adoption stalls.

risksIfYouDont.title: UNSAFE PRACTICES
risksIfYouDont.body: Unsafe practice arises when "Human in the Loop" review and approval and clinical accountability are not embedded.

risksIfYouDont.title: VENDOR DEPENDENCY
risksIfYouDont.body: Organisations remain dependent on vendors for day-to-day optimisation.

risksIfYouDont.title: GENERIC TRAINING
risksIfYouDont.body: Support does not reflect different roles, workflows or confidence levels.

risksIfYouDont.title: LOW CONFIDENCE
risksIfYouDont.body: Some users avoid AVT because they are uncomfortable with the technology.

change_adoption.description: Focus on how AVT is used in practice, not just whether it is used
change_adoption.whatIsIt: Change adoption is the extent to which AVT is used confidently and consistently in day-to-day practice beyond go-live. It involves regularly reviewing real usage and feedback to identify where support or reinforcement is needed.
change_adoption.userInsight: Adoption improved when organisations looked beyond usage data to understand user experience and variation in use, using structured pilots as learning opportunities with clear decision points rather than scaling up too early.
change_adoption.whyThisMatters:
If people don't use AVT properly, you won't get the benefits and understanding why, helps you fix issues and scale safely.
 Understanding "why not" enables targeted support for low confidence, workarounds and resistance.
 Clear adoption decision points support safe scaling and protects trust.
change_adoption.quickRealityCheck:
Is AVT being used as intended in real clinical workflows? Is use consistent across different teams and roles?
 Do staff feel confident using AVT in their day-to-day work? Do you understand why some staff are not using AVT?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: ACTIVE MONITORING
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Adoption is actively monitored using usage data and feedback from high and low users.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: TARGETED REINFORCEMENT
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Targeted support is put in place where needed to support confident and consistent use.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: LEARNING IN PRACTICE
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Use early learning to refine support and strengthen stakeholder confidence.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: VISIBLE SUPPORT
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Champions are active post go-live providing targeted support to address issues and improve adoption.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CONSISTENT USE
whatGoodLooksLike.body: AVT is used in a consistent way across teams and services in day-to-day practice.

risksIfYouDont.title: UNREALISED BENEFITS
risksIfYouDont.body: If adoption is inconsistent, the benefits of AVT will not be realised.

risksIfYouDont.title: PATCHY USE
risksIfYouDont.body: Variation in how AVT is used across teams leads to inconsistent use, reducing confidence.

risksIfYouDont.title: HIDDEN ISSUES
risksIfYouDont.body: Without understanding why people are not using AVT, underlying issues are missed.

risksIfYouDont.title: PERSISTENT WORKAROUNDS
risksIfYouDont.body: Low confidence, workarounds and resistance persist without targeted reinforcement, undermining effective use.

risksIfYouDont.title: SCALING TOO EARLY
risksIfYouDont.body: Without clear adoption insights and decision points, organisations risk scaling too quickly.

process_change.description: Make AVT part of everyday practice – set clear expectations and co-design locally
process_change.whatIsIt: Ways of Working define the new behaviours, habits and expectations needed to use AVT safely and consistently across different clinical settings.
process_change.userInsight: AVT only transformed practice when teams changed habits — otherwise old ways persisted.
process_change.whyThisMatters:
Inconsistent practice can emerge across teams and settings.
 Clinicians slip back into old habits rewriting notes or just dictation.
 Safety risks increase when "Human in the Loop" review and approval and clinical ownership drop when it gets busy.
process_change.quickRealityCheck:
Can staff explain how AVT fits with the workflow? Do supporting materials match actual practice?
 Are workarounds being spotted? Is feedback being used to refine the workflow?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: TARGETED REINFORCEMENT ACTIONS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Regular review of adoption plus feedback is used to target reinforcement actions.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: FIXED PAIN POINTS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Known pain points are fixed quickly and communicated back to users.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: ONGOING BENEFITS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Ongoing optimisation and benefits tracking continues beyond initial rollout. Benefits and successes are shared widely to reinforce value.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: AVT BECOMES ROUTINE
whatGoodLooksLike.body: AVT is embedded into everyday workflows, meetings, supervision and operational conversations.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: DATA GUIDES REINFORCEMENT
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Usage data, feedback and adoption patterns show where extra reinforcement is needed.

risksIfYouDont.title: FALLEN ADOPTION
risksIfYouDont.body: Adoption falls after initial friction because no one closes the loop.

risksIfYouDont.title: ENTRENCHED BEHAVIOURS
risksIfYouDont.body: Small irritants become entrenched behaviours and workarounds.

risksIfYouDont.title: UNPROVEN BENEFITS
risksIfYouDont.body: Benefits remain unproven and scaling loses momentum.

risksIfYouDont.title: OLD HABITS RETURN
risksIfYouDont.body: Teams revert to previous ways of working when AVT in not embedded into daily routines.

risksIfYouDont.title: ONE OFF TRAINING
risksIfYouDont.body: Staff receive go live training but no refresher support as context changes.

org_maturity.description: AVT success depends on managing adoption, not just implementation.
org_maturity.whatIsIt: Organisational Change Management Maturity helps organisations reflect on their wider ability to manage and sustain change, so change adoption strengthens long-term capability rather than adding to change fatigue.
org_maturity.userInsight: Breaking readiness into clear repeatable categories (leadership, governance, technology, people and service readiness) supported more consistent AVT success.
org_maturity.whyThisMatters:
Change maturity informs how much support and structure is needed for safe, sustained change.
 It prevents labelling organisations as being resistant, when issues are related to capability, resourcing or readiness gaps.
 It enables repeatable scaling by applying consistent readiness criteria and governance discipline.
org_maturity.quickRealityCheck:
Is AVT being managed as a people and workflow change? Is there enough change capability?
 Have stakeholders shaped the approach? Are managers and champions equipped?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: STRUCTURED READINESS
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Structured readiness criteria are used before scaling.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: USEFUL LEARNING CAPTURED
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Learning is captured and reused through evidence and examples.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: REPEATABLE CHANGE PRACTICES
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Change practices become repeatable, with clear ownership, cadence and measures.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: LEADERSHIP ALIGNMENT
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Senior leaders are aligned on why AVT matters and what success look like.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: BENEFITS ARE OWNED
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Expected benefits are clearly defined, tracked and owned beyond go live.

risksIfYouDont.title: INCONSISTENT CHANGE
risksIfYouDont.body: Change becomes reactive and inconsistent; fatigue increases as lessons are not implemented.

risksIfYouDont.title: EVIDENCE LED DECISIONS
risksIfYouDont.body: Scaling decisions become enthusiasm driven rather than evidence led.

risksIfYouDont.title: GOVERNANCE GAPS
risksIfYouDont.body: Governance and readiness gaps create avoidable disruption and loss of trust.

risksIfYouDont.title: ADOPTION NOT ACTIVELY MANAGED
risksIfYouDont.body: Focus stays on go live, with limited tracking of usage, confidence or barriers.

risksIfYouDont.title: INSUFFICIENT CHANGE CAPABILITY
risksIfYouDont.body: Teams lack the time, resource or skills to support adoption properly.

transfer_bau.description: Plan how AVT will be owned and sustained after Go-Live
transfer_bau.whatIsIt: Transfer to BAU ensures AVT moves from a time-limited rollout into routine clinical and operational practice, with clear ownership, ongoing support and sustained adoption.
transfer_bau.userInsight: Where AVT remained owned only by a project or digital team, workflow and behaviour issues resurfaced without clear operational accountability.
transfer_bau.whyThisMatters:
Without a clear BAU transition, AVT risks becoming "something we tried" rather than how we work.
 BAU ownership ensures clinical safety behaviours are maintained under everyday operational pressure.
 Embedding AVT into BAU enables continuous optimisation (templates, workflows, support) rather than freezing practice at go-live.
transfer_bau.quickRealityCheck:
Can you name who owns AVT in BAU? Is AVT being used consistently across teams?
 Do staff know where to go when something goes wrong? Are issues being fixed and improvements made?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CLEAR OWNERSHIP
whatGoodLooksLike.body: There is named BAU ownership for adoption, safety, support and optimisation.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: ACTIVE MONITORING
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Adoption, confidence and safety signals are reviewed.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Feedback loops and reinforcement activity continue after go-live, with visible fixes and updates.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: VISIBLE VALUE
whatGoodLooksLike.body: AVT performance and benefits are discussed within routine service or operational forums.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: ACCESSIBLE SUPPORT
whatGoodLooksLike.body: People know where to go for support and how to get help quickly.

risksIfYouDont.title: UNCLEAR OWNERSHIP
risksIfYouDont.body: Adoption slowly erodes as early enthusiasm fades and no one "owns" sustained use.

risksIfYouDont.title: REDUCED OVERSIGHT
risksIfYouDont.body: Safety practices (review and approval of AVT outputs and consent recording) weaken under pressure without reinforcement.

risksIfYouDont.title: PERSISTENT ISSUES
risksIfYouDont.body: Workflow and template issues persist, leading to frustration and workarounds.

risksIfYouDont.title: UNPROVEN VALUE
risksIfYouDont.body: Organisations struggle to evidence value, making further scale or funding decisions harder.

risksIfYouDont.title: LIMITED SUPPORT
risksIfYouDont.body: Support routes are unclear, so issues persist or are ignored.

celebrating_success.description: Seeing successes makes adoption feel real
celebrating_success.whatIsIt: Celebrating successes not only increases morale but it builds support among those that may need to "see it to believe it". Recognition is needed in order to cement or reinforce the change.
celebrating_success.userInsight: Celebrating success was most effective when staff saw what worked from their peers, as real examples from colleagues strengthened engagement and adoption.
celebrating_success.whyThisMatters:
Saying exactly what went well helps everyone feel proud and ready for the next step.
 It creates a culture of appreciation where people feel valued, recognised and encouraged to keep improving.
 It reinforces positive behaviours by showing what good looks like and encouraging others to follow it.
celebrating_success.quickRealityCheck:
Are you celebrating genuine progress, not just activity? Are you recognising small and large successes?
 Do you have a criteria for what success looks like? Are you learning from successes and not just measuring them?

whatGoodLooksLike.title: PROGRESS IS MADE VISIBLE
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Achievements are shared clearly so people can see what has improved and why it matters.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: USEFUL LEARNING CAPTURED
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Celebrating success includes reflecting on what worked well, so the learning can be used again.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: PEOPLE RECOGNITION
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Recognise the people behind the success, including quieter contributions and team effort.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: SUCCESS MEASURES DEFINED
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Clear definitions for measuring success is shared and understood.

whatGoodLooksLike.title: TIMELY RECOGNITION
whatGoodLooksLike.body: Success is acknowledged soon after it happens, so staff feel their contribution has been noticed and valued.

risksIfYouDont.title: MOTIVATION DROPS
risksIfYouDont.body: People may feel their effort goes unnoticed, which can reduce energy, commitment and enthusiasm.

risksIfYouDont.title: PROGRESS BECOMES INVISIBLE
risksIfYouDont.body: Without celebration, improvements and achievements can be overlooked or forgotten.

risksIfYouDont.title: LEARNING IS LOST
risksIfYouDont.body: If AVT does not pause to recognise success, it may also miss the opportunity to understand what worked well.

risksIfYouDont.title: CONFIDENCE IS REDUCED
risksIfYouDont.body: Staff may be less likely to take initiative or try new approaches if success is not acknowledged.

risksIfYouDont.title: TEAM SPIRIT WEAKENS
risksIfYouDont.body: A lack of recognition can reduce shared pride, connection and collaboration across AVT.
